objectives: I can understand when someone talks about their day in Simple Past.
I can describe my own yesterday to a partner in 3 or more sentences.
I can use Simple Past correctly for regular and irregular verbs.

stages.name: Opening — retrieval and bridge
stages.purpose: Recall Simple Past forms and prepositions from the previous two lessons before today's listening and speaking work.

procedure.text: Quick fire (whole class, oral): call out base verbs one at a time — go, eat, do, have, see. Pupils call back the Simple Past form. Accept any correct attempt; do not correct yet.
Prepositions cued recall (3 sentences on board): 'I wake up ___ 7 o'clock.' / 'I go to school ___ the morning.' / 'We have sport ___ Monday.' Pupils answer in chorus.
Think-write: 'Write one sentence about what you did last weekend. Use Simple Past.' Pupils write in exercise books.
Partner swap: pupils check each other's verb form. Teacher circulates and notes the most common error on paper — use it in Stage 2.

Bridge (spoken): 'Last two lessons you learned the Simple Past and prepositions for time. Today you put them together: first you listen to two people describe their Tuesday, then you describe YOUR own yesterday to your partner.' Write the two I-can statements on the board and read them aloud.

stages.name: Grammar recap — Simple Past
stages.purpose: Briefly revisit the Simple Past rule and the German Perfekt contrast before pupils meet it in extended listening input.

procedure.text: Display the grammar recap sheet. Point to the rule: regular (-ed) and the six irregular forms. Address the error you noted in Stage 1 on the board.

Highlight the German contrast on the sheet: 'In German: Ich habe gegessen — two words. In English: I ate — one word. No have when telling a story.' Read two sentences aloud from the dialogue pupils are about to hear.
Pupils write the six irregular forms (went, had, did, ate, saw, was/were) in their vocab column. 30 seconds.

stages.name: Listening — Tom and Lisa's Tuesday
stages.purpose: Build understanding of spoken Simple Past in context using two structured listen runs with a comprehension grid.

procedure.text: Set the scene: 'You will hear two friends, Tom and Lisa, talking about their Tuesday. Draw a quick grid in your book: four rows — Morning, Lunchtime, After school, Evening — and two columns — Tom, Lisa.'
Listen run 1 (gist): teacher reads the dialogue at natural pace. Pupils listen only, no writing. After: ask 'Who had a busier afternoon — Tom or Lisa?' Pupils answer orally.
Pupils write their gist answer (one word: Tom or Lisa) in their book.
Listen run 2 (detail): teacher reads the dialogue again, more slowly, pausing briefly at each new time section. Pupils fill in the grid with short notes.
Pupils complete their grid. Short notes only — they do not need to write full sentences.

Partner compare grids. Then class reveal: teacher reads grid answers aloud (Morning: Tom got up late, had milk, took bus / Lisa woke up at 6:30, had toast + banana, walked. Lunchtime: Tom went home, had soup / Lisa had sandwich in canteen. After school: Tom did homework, watched TV / Lisa went to football. Evening: Tom bed at 9:30, tired / Lisa read a book, bed at 9). Pupils self-correct in a different colour.

stages.name: Speaking — pair dialogue, frame-fade
stages.purpose: Move from receptive understanding to genuine oral production of Simple Past, using sentence frames faded after the first round.

procedure.text: Write frames on the board: 'What did you do yesterday?' / 'I woke up at...' / 'Then I...' / 'After that I...' / 'Finally I...' / 'In the evening I...'. Model one full exchange with a volunteer.
Round 1 (frames visible): Partner A asks 'What did you do yesterday?' Partner B answers using at least 3 frames. Then swap roles. Both partners speak.
Erase all frames from the board. Tell pupils: 'Now try without the frames. The structure is the same — you remember it.'
Round 2 (no frames): same dialogue with a new partner if possible, or swap roles with the same partner. Teacher circulates and notes the top 2 errors.
Write the top 2 errors as full sentences on the board. Ask the class to identify and fix them together.

stages.name: Wrap-up — self-assess and exit ticket
stages.purpose: Return to the learning intentions for self-assessment and collect a brief written sample as a formative check.

procedure.text: Point to the I-can statements on the board. Pupils rate themselves: thumbs up (confident), sideways (mostly), down (need more practice). Note the rough split.
Exit ticket: 'Write 2 sentences in Simple Past about YOUR yesterday. You have 3 minutes.' Pupils write in exercise books.
Pupils hand in books open at the exit ticket page, or teacher photographs the pages. Not graded — formative check only.
Preview: 'Next lesson: word order in Simple Past sentences with time expressions, and more speaking practice.'
Early finishers: open the gap-fill exercise on the class page.

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: keep board frames visible during Round 2 of speaking; allow 1 sentence for exit ticket. Stronger pupils: in Round 2, partner asks follow-up questions (Why? / Who with? / How long?); exit ticket requires 3 sentences, at least one including a time expression.
exercisePlan: gap_fill: 6 sentences from the Tom-and-Lisa dialogue, key irregular Simple Past verbs blanked, full word bank — fallback activity for early finishers and next-lesson review [fk.g.simple_past, fk.k.hoer.3]
